metadata.description: Index and navigation guide for convention cards, disclosure requirements, and partnership documentation in the BridgeLab Knowledge Base.

headings.title: American Contract Bridge League (ACBL) Convention Card

metadata.title: Aspro Convention
metadata.description: An aggressive conventional defense to an opponent's 1NT opening that emphasizes showing the major suits first while allowing efficient description of one- and two-suited hands.

metadata.title: Balancing Double
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Balancing Double (Protective Double), including theory, hand requirements, responses, competitive strategy, expert agreements, and modern treatments.

metadata.title: Balancing Notrump
metadata.description: A natural notrump overcall in the balancing seat that shows a balanced hand with values insufficient for a direct notrump overcall, allowing the partnership to compete accurately after the opponents stop bidding.

metadata.title: Competitive Bidding
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to competitive bidding in Contract Bridge, covering overcalls, doubles, cue bids, balancing, sacrifices, and modern expert competitive methods.

metadata.title: Brozel Convention
metadata.description: An advanced conventional defense against a 1NT opening that uses artificial overcalls to show one-suited and two-suited hands, allowing the partnership to compete aggressively and accurately.

metadata.title: Cappelletti Convention
metadata.description: A conventional defense against an opponent's 1NT opening that uses artificial overcalls to describe one-suited and two-suited hands while competing aggressively for the partscore or game.

metadata.title: DONT Convention
metadata.description: A conventional defense against an opponent's 1NT opening using Double and artificial overcalls to describe one-suited and two-suited hands while competing efficiently.

metadata.title: Equal Level Conversion Doubles (ELCD)
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to Equal Level Conversion Doubles (ELCD), an expert extension of takeout doubles that permits equal-level suit corrections without implying extra strength.

metadata.title: Equal Level Conversion (ELC)
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Equal Level Conversion convention, an advanced extension of takeout doubles that allows the doubler to convert partner's forced minor-suit response into another suit without showing extra strength.

metadata.title: Fit Jump Shift
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Fit Jump Shift convention, a competitive bidding treatment showing support for partner's suit together with a long side suit and offensive values.

headings.title: Fit Jump Shift vs Mixed Raise
Fit Jump Shift vs Weak Jump Shift

metadata.title: Jump Shift
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to Jump Shift bidding, covering natural, strong, weak, and artificial jump shifts, expert treatments, partnership agreements, and modern applications.

headings.title: Assuming Every Jump Shift Is Strong

metadata.title: Ghestem Convention
metadata.description: An advanced three-suited conventional defense that uses three different artificial overcalls to show every possible two-suited hand after an opponent's opening bid.

headings.title: Forgetting Which Two Suits Are Shown

metadata.title: Hamilton Convention
metadata.description: A conventional defense against a 1NT opening that uses two-level bids to show one-suited and two-suited hands, allowing the partnership to compete effectively against notrump.

metadata.title: Landy Convention
metadata.description: A conventional defense against a 1NT opening in which a 2♣ overcall shows both major suits, allowing the partnership to compete effectively and locate major-suit fits.

headings.title: Competition After the Major Is Chosen

metadata.title: Meckwell Convention
metadata.description: An aggressive conventional defense against an opponent's 1NT opening developed by Jeff Meckstroth and Eric Rodwell, using highly descriptive artificial bids to show one- and two-suited hands.

metadata.title: Michaels Cue Bid
metadata.description: An artificial cue bid over an opponent's opening that shows a two-suited hand, allowing the partnership to compete aggressively while efficiently describing distribution.

headings.title: Responses After a Minor Cue Bid
Responses After a Major Cue Bid

metadata.title: Multi-Landy Convention
metadata.description: An advanced defense against a 1NT opening that combines the simplicity of Landy with the flexibility of Cappelletti/Hamilton to show both one-suited and two-suited hands.

metadata.title: Negative Free Bid
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Negative Free Bid (NFB) convention, an advanced competitive treatment that distinguishes constructive hands from forcing hands after opponent interference.

headings.title: When to Use Negative Free Bid

metadata.title: Responsive Cue Bid
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Responsive Cue Bid convention, an expert competitive bidding treatment used after partner's takeout double and the opponents raise their suit.

headings.title: Responsive Cue Bid After Minor Openings
Responsive Cue Bid After Major Openings

metadata.title: Top and Bottom Cue Bid
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Top and Bottom Cue Bid convention, an advanced competitive bidding method used to distinguish one-suited and two-suited hands over an opponent's opening.

metadata.title: Unusual Notrump
metadata.description: An artificial 2NT overcall showing the two lowest unbid suits, allowing the partnership to compete aggressively with distributional hands after an opponent's opening bid.

metadata.title: Unusual vs. Unusual
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Unusual vs. Unusual (UvU) convention, an advanced defensive method used after opponents employ the Unusual Notrump convention to distinguish raises, cue bids, and suit bids.

metadata.title: Weak Jump Overcalls
metadata.description: A preemptive overcall made by jumping in a suit over an opponent's opening bid, showing a long suit with limited high-card strength and designed to disrupt the opponents' auction.

metadata.title: Western Cue Bid
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Western Cue Bid convention, an expert treatment used to investigate the possibility of playing 3NT by asking partner for a stopper in the opponents' suit.

metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to defensive bidding in Contract Bridge, covering methods used to compete against opponents' opening bids, artificial systems, and conventional defenses.

metadata.title: CRASH Convention
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the CRASH (Color-RAnk-SHape) convention, an expert defense against Strong Club and Strong Notrump systems using two-suited overcalls.

metadata.title: Defense Against Multi 2♦
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to defending against the Multi 2♦ convention, including standard and expert methods, balancing, doubles, overcalls, responses, and partnership agreements.

metadata.title: Suction Convention
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Suction Convention, an advanced expert defense against Strong 1NT and Strong Club openings using artificial overcalls.

metadata.title: TWERB
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the TWERB convention, an expert defense against artificial and natural opening bids using transfer overcalls.

metadata.title: Action Double
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the modern expert Action Double, a competitive double requesting partner to take intelligent action when neither passing nor bidding is attractive.

metadata.title: Doubles
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to conventional doubles in Contract Bridge, covering takeout, penalty, competitive, lead-directing, and expert partnership doubles.

metadata.title: Do Something Intelligent (DSI)
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the DSI (Do Something Intelligent) principle, an expert competitive bidding philosophy emphasizing partnership judgment over rigid bidding rules.

metadata.title: Maximal Double
metadata.description: A conventional double used in competitive auctions after the opponents have competed below game, showing a game invitation with trump support when no room remains for a natural game try.

headings.title: Using a Maximal Double Without a Fit

metadata.title: Negative Double
metadata.description: A conventional double made by responder after an opponent's overcall, typically showing unbid suits rather than penalty interest.

headings.title: Using the Double Instead of a Natural Bid

metadata.title: Penalty Double
metadata.description: A double that expresses the intention to defend the doubled contract, expecting the opponents to fail and produce a profitable penalty.

headings.title: Penalty Double of a Suit Contract

metadata.title: Reopening Double
metadata.description: A conventional double made after the opponents' auction appears ready to end, showing values and a desire to keep the auction alive rather than defend.

metadata.title: Responsive Double
metadata.description: A conventional double made after partner has made a takeout double and the opponents have raised their suit, showing values and interest in the unbid suits.

metadata.title: Support Double
metadata.description: A conventional double by opener after responder bids a new suit and the opponents interfere, showing exactly three-card support for responder's suit.

metadata.title: Takeout Double
metadata.description: A conventional double of an opponent's opening bid that asks partner to bid an unbid suit rather than defend the doubled contract.

metadata.title: Ekren Convention
metadata.description: An artificial weak 2♦ opening showing both major suits, typically 4-4, 4-5, or 5-4 distribution with preemptive values.

metadata.title: Flannery Convention
metadata.description: An artificial 2♦ opening showing exactly five hearts and four spades with opening values, designed to solve rebid problems after opening one heart.

metadata.title: Gambling 3NT
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Gambling 3NT convention, including requirements, responses, variations, defenses, expert treatments, and partnership agreements.

metadata.title: Opening Bids
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to opening bids in Contract Bridge, covering natural openings, preempts, strong openings, hand evaluation, partnership style, and modern bidding principles.

metadata.title: Namyats Convention
metadata.description: An artificial preemptive convention in which a 4♣ opening shows a strong four-heart hand and a 4♦ opening shows a strong four-spade hand.

metadata.title: Multi 2♦ Convention
metadata.description: An artificial 2♦ opening showing one of several possible hand types, most commonly a weak two in either major, while preserving bidding space and increasing preemptive pressure.

metadata.title: Kokish Relay
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Kokish Relay, an expert relay treatment after a strong 2♣ opening that distinguishes balanced hands from strong one-suited and two-suited hands while conserving bidding space.

metadata.title: Relay Bidding
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to Relay Bidding, one of the most sophisticated bidding methods in bridge, using artificial relay bids to exchange highly accurate information about shape, strength, controls, and distribution.

metadata.title: Relay Bidding
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to relay bidding in Contract Bridge, covering relay principles, step responses, relay techniques, and advanced relay systems.

metadata.title: Relay Principle
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Relay Principle, the foundation of modern relay bidding systems, including philosophy, structure, relay auctions, responses, advantages, disadvantages, and expert applications.

metadata.title: Spiral Relay
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Spiral Relay principle, an advanced relay-bidding technique used to identify suit length, honor location, and hand pattern through cyclic step responses.

metadata.title: Step Responses
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to Step Responses, the foundation of relay bidding systems, explaining step structures, response scales, applications, and expert partnership agreements.

metadata.title: 2NT Inquiry after Multi 2♦
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the artificial 2NT inquiry used after a Multi 2♦ opening to identify opener's hand type, strength, and suit.

metadata.title: 2NT Inquiry over Weak Two
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the 2NT Inquiry convention used after partner's Weak Two opening to evaluate game and slam potential.

headings.title: Choosing Between Feature Ask and Ogust

metadata.title: Jacoby 2NT
metadata.description: A game-forcing response to a major-suit opening that shows four-card trump support and opening values, allowing the partnership to investigate slam while keeping the auction low.

headings.title: Using Jacoby with Only Three Trumps

metadata.title: Bergen Raises
metadata.description: A convention that uses jump responses after a major-suit opening to distinguish constructive, invitational, and preemptive raises while conserving bidding space.

metadata.title: Checkback Stayman
metadata.description: A conventional rebid used after a 1NT rebid by opener to determine whether opener holds three-card support for responder's major or an unshown four-card major.

metadata.title: Drury Convention
metadata.description: A conventional response by a passed hand to a third- or fourth-seat major-suit opening, showing a limit raise with three or more-card support while allowing opener to distinguish between a light and full opening.

headings.title: Using Drury Without Being a Passed Hand

metadata.title: Feature Ask
metadata.description: An artificial 2NT inquiry after a Weak Two opening that asks opener to show an outside feature rather than describe hand strength or suit quality.

headings.title: Showing Honors in the Trump Suit

metadata.title: Fourth Suit Forcing
metadata.description: An artificial bid of the only unbid suit after three suits have been bid naturally, forcing partner to bid again and requesting additional information about strength, shape, and stoppers.

headings.title: Fourth Suit Forcing vs New Minor Forcing
Treating the Fourth Suit as Natural

metadata.title: Inverted Minors
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Inverted Minors convention, an artificial response structure that exchanges the meanings of the single and double raise after a minor-suit opening.

metadata.title: Lebensohl after 1NT Doubled
metadata.description: Conventional agreements used when an opponent doubles partner's 1NT opening, allowing responder to distinguish weak escape hands, invitational values, and penalty-oriented hands.

metadata.title: Lebensohl after a 1NT Overcall
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Lebensohl convention used after partner's 1NT overcall of the opponents' opening bid.

metadata.title: Lebensohl Convention
metadata.description: An artificial convention used after interference over a 1NT opening or after partner's takeout double, allowing responder to distinguish weak, invitational, and game-forcing hands while showing or denying a stopper in the opponent's suit.

headings.title: Using Lebensohl in the Wrong Auction

metadata.title: Minor Suit Stayman
metadata.description: A convention used after a 1NT opening to investigate minor-suit fits, distinguish between notrump and minor-suit games, and explore slam when no major-suit fit exists.

headings.title: Using the Convention With Weak Hands

metadata.title: Mixed Raise
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Mixed Raise convention, an expert treatment showing constructive values with trump support in competitive auctions.

headings.title: Treating It as a Limit Raise

metadata.title: New Minor Forcing
metadata.description: An artificial convention in which responder bids the unbid minor after opener rebids 1NT, forcing opener to further describe the hand and helping the partnership locate major-suit fits or the best notrump contract.

metadata.title: Ogust Convention
metadata.description: An artificial response convention used after a Weak Two opening to distinguish minimum and maximum hands as well as suit quality, helping responder judge game prospects.

metadata.title: Passed-Hand Bergen Raises
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to Passed-Hand Bergen Raises, an advanced extension of Bergen Raises used by a passed hand after partner opens a major in third or fourth seat.

metadata.title: Passed-Hand Jacoby
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Passed-Hand Jacoby convention, a constructive raise used by a passed hand to show strong trump support and game interest without shortness.

metadata.title: Passed Hand Splinter
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Passed Hand Splinter convention, showing a fit, shortness, and constructive values after responder has previously passed.

headings.title: Treating It as a Standard Splinter

metadata.title: Puppet Stayman
metadata.description: An advanced Stayman variation used after a 2NT opening or a strong notrump sequence to locate 5-3 and 4-4 major-suit fits while preserving bidding space for game and slam exploration.

headings.title: Confusing Puppet Stayman with Standard Stayman

metadata.title: Response to Gambling 3NT
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to responding after partner opens a Gambling 3NT, including sign-off methods, slam investigation, and partnership agreements.

metadata.title: Responses
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to responder's first actions after partner's opening bid, covering natural responses, conventional responses, forcing methods, raises, and partnership agreements.

metadata.title: Reverse Drury
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Reverse Drury convention, an advanced variation of Drury used by a passed hand to distinguish stronger constructive raises after a third- or fourth-seat major opening.

metadata.title: Rubensohl Convention
metadata.description: An advanced transfer-based extension of Lebensohl used after interference over partner's 1NT opening, allowing responder to distinguish weak, invitational, and game-forcing hands while efficiently showing suit length and stopper status.

metadata.title: Smolen Convention
metadata.description: An extension of Stayman used after a 1NT opening that allows responder with game-forcing values and a 5-4 major-suit distribution to reveal the five-card major while preserving the strong hand as declarer.

metadata.title: Soloway Jump Shifts
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Soloway Jump Shifts convention, a modern expert treatment using strong jump shifts to establish a game force while preserving bidding space for constructive exploration.

metadata.title: Splinter Convention
metadata.description: A double jump response that shows four-card or longer trump support, game-forcing values, and a singleton or void in the bid suit.

metadata.title: Stayman
metadata.description: A conventional response to a 1NT or 2NT opening used to locate a four-card major-suit fit and improve game and slam bidding.

metadata.title: Swiss Raise
metadata.description: A jump response to a major-suit opening that shows a game-forcing raise with four-card support and slam interest, using one level less than a direct jump to game.

headings.title: Using Swiss Raise with Invitational Hands

metadata.title: Two-Way Checkback
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Two-Way Checkback convention, an advanced artificial checkback system used after opener rebids 1NT to distinguish invitational and game-forcing hands while investigating major-suit fits and notrump contracts.

headings.title: Confusing Two-Way Checkback with Two-Way NMF

metadata.title: Two-Way New Minor Forcing
metadata.description: Comprehensive guide to the Two-Way New Minor Forcing convention, an advanced continuation used after opener rebids 1NT to distinguish invitational and game-forcing hands.

metadata.title: Blackwood Convention
metadata.description: A slam-investigation convention using 4NT to ask for Aces (or Key Cards in modern variants), helping partnerships determine whether a slam contract is safe.

metadata.title: Cue Bidding
metadata.description: A family of conventional bids in which a player bids the opponents' suit or a previously bid suit to convey artificial information, most commonly to show controls during slam investigation or to indicate a strong hand in competitive auctions.

metadata.title: DOPI and ROPI
metadata.description: Conventional methods for responding to interference over Blackwood or Roman Key Card Blackwood, allowing the partnership to continue ace-asking despite opponent interference.

metadata.title: Gerber Convention
metadata.description: An artificial 4♣ bid used primarily after notrump auctions to ask partner for the number of Aces, allowing the partnership to investigate slam while preserving bidding space.

metadata.title: Roman Key Card Blackwood (RKCB)
metadata.description: A modern slam-investigation convention that uses 4NT to ask for the five key cards—the four Aces and the King of the agreed trump suit—and optionally the trump Queen.

metadata.description: An artificial response to a 1NT or 2NT opening that transfers opener into responder's five-card or longer major suit while keeping the strong notrump hand as declarer.

metadata.title: Texas Transfer
metadata.description: An artificial response to a 1NT or 2NT opening that transfers opener to a major suit at the game level, allowing responder to conceal the stronger hand and simplify game and slam auctions.
